newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nervous Belgian bonds seen flat after rebound.
newsitem.headline: Nervous Belgian bonds seen flat after rebound.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which recouped Thursday's losses in active business on Friday, are set to trade sideways on Monday and Tuesday in view of the upcoming OLO auction and expected U.S. interest rate rise, traders said.
"With Monday's auction and the likely rate decision on Tuesday it would be dangerous to take a position," one trader said. "So the market will be flat early next week."
Traders said the market had already factored in a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates at Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee.
"If it is 25 points the market will move up again. Only if it is more will the market not take it kindly," one trader said.
Traders said there was activity all along the yield curve, but it was particularly noticeable in the 10-year benchmark BE286= and the longer maturities.
"There was really very good volume. The longer end was very well bid. It flattened compared with yesterday," one trader said. "The benchmark was also active."
Traders said an added element of uncertainty was Monday's Belgian bond auction. They did not expect the Treasury to offer much of OLOs 25 and 26 at the auction.
Added to this is an estimated 40 to 50 billion francs worth of coupons coming to maturity on March 28.

"I expect most of this to come back into the market, which will provide good support," one trader said. "If it doesn't come back it will be bad for bonds, but I expect it to. It essentially has nowhere else to go. We will see on Tuesday."
"It is mainly insurance and pension funds so I expect they will reinvest in this market," another trader said.
The yield of the benchmark March 2007 OLO ended Friday at 6.07 percent, down from Thursday's closing 6.11. The spread over German Bunds was 14 basis points, down from Thursday's 16.
"It could widen a bit against early next week," one trader said.
The March futures contract ended Friday 37 basis points higher at 120.32, reversing Thursday's losses. June futures were up 36 basis points at 119.44.
